### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**2** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **231** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **166** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **166**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **107** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **171** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 33bad96192fe929916ac068f84c32abcf6207180` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `76a803a040396544ca7a5ece36c29fb4858a2af0` — the merge of head `311ea586b7e0fc474b7d852c50e40f00e5a9f1ad` into base `33bad96192fe929916ac068f84c32abcf6207180`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 76a803a040396544ca7a5ece36c29fb4858a2af0 && git checkout 76a803a040396544ca7a5ece36c29fb4858a2af0
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 33bad96192fe929916ac068f84c32abcf6207180 311ea586b7e0fc474b7d852c50e40f00e5a9f1ad && git checkout -B drift-repro 33bad96192fe929916ac068f84c32abcf6207180 && git merge --no-ff 311ea586b7e0fc474b7d852c50e40f00e5a9f1ad

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 33bad96192fe929916ac068f84c32abcf6207180
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `2bc349660840b5f927484039243bb5102c2d4dbb`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts + none

PR #32114, card #32078. Inputs: the card body and its four comments (triage `6761127384`, claim `6761322650`, amendment `6761379000`, dev report `6762274922`), the PR body, the three-file net diff against `main` (merge base `fe1249b7`; `main` at `33bad961` has not touched either spec file since), and the head's check-runs. No file in the diff implements the contract: the runtime binder and `connector-pull.ts` are #32071's and are untouched, so they were read, not reviewed. The test file and the changeset are the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

Check-runs at the time of this record. Concluded `success`: Check Changeset, Spec property liveness, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, Dogfood Regression Gate, Check PR Size, Flag docs affected by code changes, Plan Test Core shards, Plan Test UI shards, Auto Label, filter. **Still `in_progress`, so not judged here:** Build Core, Build UI Deps, Test Core 1/8 to 8/8, Live E2E UI, Type Check · source gates / consumer gates / debt ledger / workspace, Lint · ESLint / docs & code guards / CI, release & engine gates / repo & tooling gates / scoped · query-options erasure / scoped · slot lookup & corpus. None has concluded red. This verdict rests on the concluded runs and the read; the type-level pins (`check:test-typecheck`) and the vitest pins are answered only when Type Check and Test Core conclude, and a red there is not covered by this PASS.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept set of `ConnectorSourcePullRequest`: widened, right.** One new optional member, `callerPackageId?: string | null`. Every request that typed before still types; no member is removed, renamed or tightened. A caller that builds the request and an implementation that takes it (`service-automation` `engine.ts` L2874, L5256, L5270, the only non-test consumers in the tree) both compile unchanged.
- **Accept set of `IAutomationService.pullConnectorSource`: unchanged in behaviour, right.** No implementation reads the key at this head (`connector-pull.ts` still reads `protocol.getMetaItem({ type: 'mapping', name })`; the binder still sends `{ mapping, context }`, `app-artifact-handlers.ts` L1000). The diff publishes a type and a doc, no behaviour.
- **Public surface: one member on an already-exported interface, right.** `api-surface/contracts.json` L77 and `export-origins/contracts.json` L77 record the interface by symbol only, so neither baseline moves. The card's pin "the conformance and API baselines are updated" is met by there being nothing to update: the interface has no zod twin and no conformance baseline in the tree.
- **`Metadata-protocol: none`: right.** The key is a service-request field the runtime fills; `JobSchema.pull`, `MappingSchema` and `connectorSource` are untouched, and Spec property liveness is green.
- **Spelling and type: right.** `OwnershipQueueCallerPackage` (`ownership-queue-service.ts` L125) is `string | null`, optional on all three reads, with "Omitted, `null` or `''`" as the no-package value. The resolver agrees (`packages/core/src/package-scoped-resolution.ts` L609–616: a non-string or `''` caller is `null` and takes the environment-wide branch). The bare `packageId` in the sibling contracts names an owning package, so it was right not to reuse it.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/spec` `patch`, with `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` on both the PR body and the changeset. It matches what the diff publishes: an optional member, no protocol change, no narrowing. It is the level of the precedent `.changeset/31734-queue-caller-package.md` (the same key on the ownership-queue reads, `patch`). Check Changeset concluded `success`.

Clause-②: yes (widening) — correct. No narrowing arm is owed here: the D3 (a) and (c) refusals arrive with the reader that wires the key (#32071), and that card declares and measures them.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty. Nothing to answer or escalate.
- `deviations` (two, both harness-step skips: no assignee or review request on `pr_create`; a model-free commit trailer): accepted. Neither touches the diff.
- `out_of_scope_findings` (one, `carrier: none`, the `driver-turso` dist missing from the `runtime^...` build closure): a build-closure artefact of the dev's box, not of this change. Accepted as noted; the Type Check lanes on the head are the record.
- Claim file surface (`ConnectorSourcePullRequest` only, its test, its changeset; ⛔ no binder, no `connector-pull.ts`, no `ExecutionContext`): held. The file list is exactly those three paths.
- The epic's red-line review before landing is the seat's, not this record's.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts`, judged against ADR-0150 D3, the precedent it cites and its first consumer (#32071, the binder at `app-artifact-handlers.ts` L955–1002 and the read at `connector-pull.ts` L266–273).

The field holds. The type, the optionality, the three absent spellings and the two resolution arms agree with D3's text and with the resolver, sentence by sentence. An implementation written before the key satisfies the contract, as the doc says. The key advertises nothing the runtime fails to deliver, because the doc says a pre-key implementation reads by no package.

Findings:

1. **should-fix — the doc's "own item" inference is false for a multi-package artifact, and so is "the job's package, its `appId`".** The doc says: "The job binder already requires the mapping to be declared in the job's own bundle, so read from that package the name answers the package's own item." The step from bundle to package does not hold. `judgeJobPull` looks the mapping up in `collectBundleMappings(bundle)`, which reads through `resolveArtifactCollections` (`packages/runtime/src/artifact-collections.ts` L457): for an artifact with `packages[]` (ADR-0130 D4) that is the merge of EVERY package body's `mappings`. One `AppPlugin` schedules all of that artifact's jobs under one `appId`, the top-level `manifest.id` (`app-plugin.ts` L500, L1877). So a job declared in package body A whose mapping sits in body B binds today, and read by D3 from `appId` the name is not A's own item. D3 (c) and N1 (record `6729820123`) say a sibling package of the same artifact is in the closure only when declared, so that read is step 2 or an `outside-closure` refusal, not `own`. Even a job and mapping in the same body are not `own` when `appId` is the artifact's id and not that body's. The card states the same inference ("D3 therefore always answers `own`, and every one-holder answer stays as it is"), and #32071 would read this sentence as its ground for declaring no narrowing. Not measured here: how many first-party multi-package artifacts carry a pull job (read-only review). Fix, on the TSDoc only: either scope the sentence to a single-package artifact, or drop it and say that the caller's package is the package that DECLARES the job, leaving which id the binder passes to #32071. The member, its type and the two arms need no change. The fix moves the head, so it earns a delta review; #32071 should measure the multi-package case and declare its `Narrowing:` line on that measurement, not on this sentence.
2. **nit — "exactly as today" names two different reads.** The doc equates the absent value with "the bare name, read as a caller with no package". At this head the bare read is `getMetaItem` (first registered wins); D3's caller-less read is one holder or a refusal naming the candidates (409). They differ when two packages hold the name, and the card says #32071 moves the absent case to the second. The sentence is true at this head and stops being literally true when the reader lands, and the doc pin's regex fixes the wording. Follow-up on #32071: reword it there with the reader, as the precedent does ("the environment-wide read", with its two-holder refusal stated).
3. **nit — the package-id arm omits the two outcomes D3 treats apart.** "else a refusal naming every candidate" folds in a name nobody holds (`not-found`, no candidates) and D3 (a) (a package caller is refused a name only the environment holds). The precedent's type doc spells these out. The binder's bundle check makes them unreachable for a job's pull on a single-package artifact, so nothing is wrong today. Accepted deviation, or one clause with finding 1's fix.

Read but not reviewed (lane seat's ACCEPT): the test file's pins match the contract as written. Note for the delta: the doc pin does not cover the sentence in finding 1, so the fix needs no test change unless the seat wants it pinned.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-mrax3v`
Reviewed-by: `session_01WGufzh7cM8EmUX4T2CBNHX` (isolated contract-review sub-agent of the seat's session; did not write the diff)

**VERDICT: PASS**

No must-fix. Finding 1 is a should-fix: its fix owes a delta review on the new head, and this record covers `2bc34966` only. The pending check-runs listed above are not covered.

## Contract review — delta

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `311ea586b7e0fc474b7d852c50e40f00e5a9f1ad`
Delta-of: 6762357312
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts + none

Delta read: `2bc34966..311ea586`, three hunks — the `callerPackageId` TSDoc, one doc-pin line in the test, one changeset sentence. The member, its type and its optionality are byte-identical to the reviewed head; the PR's file list is still the same three paths. ①, ② and ③ of the record this follows stand unchanged: the accept set, the `patch` level and `Clause-②: yes (widening)` are not touched by a doc-only delta.

### Finding by finding

1. **should-fix 1 — closed.** The false inference is gone. The doc now says the caller's package is "the package that declares the job", drops `appId`, and states the opposite of what it claimed before: the read is not inferred to answer that package's own mapping, because in an artifact of several packages the binder finds the mapping in any package body, so the name may resolve through the closure or be refused as outside it. That agrees with the code it describes (`judgeJobPull` over `resolveArtifactCollections`' merge of every `packages[]` body) and with D3 (c) / N1. Which id the binder passes is left to #32071, as asked. The changeset sentence carries the same wording. #32071 still owes its own measurement of the multi-package case for its `Narrowing:` line; this doc no longer gives it a reason to skip one.
2. **nit 3 — closed.** The package-id arm now separates the outcomes: a name nothing in the environment holds is not found; a name held twice in the reach, held only by a package outside it, or held only by an environment-authored item (D3 (a)) is a refusal naming every candidate. Each clause matches the resolver (`packages/core/src/package-scoped-resolution.ts` L620–640: `ambiguous-in-closure`, `outside-closure` with the environment pushed as a candidate, `not-found` when there are no candidates).
3. **nit 2 — unchanged, stays accepted.** "exactly as today — the bare name, read as a caller with no package" is the same sentence, true at this head, and still pinned by the same regex. It is reworded on #32071 with the reader.

Nothing new introduced. The doc pin swapped its `appId` assertion for a regex on "the package that declares the job", which the new TSDoc satisfies across its line break; the other three doc assertions still match the text. Residual, no grade: the changeset keeps the short form "else a refusal naming every candidate" where the TSDoc now spells the outcomes apart — changeset prose, not reviewed. The PR body may still say `appId`; the tree is what was judged.

### Check-runs on `311ea586`

Nothing has concluded yet. `in_progress`: Check Changeset, Spec property liveness, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Check PR Size, Flag docs affected by code changes. The build, Test Core, Type Check and Lint lanes had not registered a run on this head when read. No gate verdict exists for this head, so this delta is judged on the read alone; a red on any of them, the doc pin in Test Core included, is not covered by this PASS.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-mrax3v`
Reviewed-by: `session_01WGufzh7cM8EmUX4T2CBNHX` (isolated contract-review sub-agent of the seat's session; did not write the diff)

**VERDICT: PASS**

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：连接器拉取的请求契约 `ConnectorSourcePullRequest` 新增一个可选字段 `callerPackageId`（`string | null`），用来携带调用方的包；对作业的拉取来说，就是声明该作业的包。
- 为什么改：ADR-0150 D3 要求按 `(包, 名称)` 解析 mapping；#32071 之后，同名 mapping 有两个持有者时，按裸名读会返回 409，作业的包必须能传到拉取这一步。
- 风险与回滚：只是放宽，而且只改了类型和文档：至今没有任何实现读取这个字段，不传（省略、`null` 或 `''`）时与今天完全一致。回滚即还原本 PR。
- 先看：`packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts` 里该字段的 TSDoc。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec exec vitest run src/contracts/automation-service.test.ts`，预期 20/20 全绿。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地。

席位意见：fable 契约复审 PASS（6762357312），唯一的建议改是 TSDoc 里「必定读到本包条目」的推断，在多包制品里不成立，已经改掉，增量复审 PASS（6762454953）。剩下一条 nit（「exactly as today」这句会在 #32071 落地后过时），随 #32071 一起改。

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT · domain:spec#3 · head `311ea586b7e0fc474b7d852c50e40f00e5a9f1ad`

- **Shape:** 3 files (+103 −1), merge base `fe1249b7`. The diff adds one optional member `callerPackageId?: string | null` on `ConnectorSourcePullRequest`, with TSDoc for both arms; type-level and doc pins in `automation-service.test.ts`; and an `@objectstack/spec` patch changeset.
- **Premise measured:** at `fe1249b7`, the interface (L1066) carried only `mapping`, `context?` and `environmentId?` (claim 6761322650).
- **Gates:**
  - Check-runs on this head: 58 success, 13 skipped, 0 red. `mergeable_state` is clean.
  - The two reds on the superseded head `2bc34966` were aggregators whose lanes were cancelled by the push; that head was not judged.
  - Dev report 6762274922 (on `2bc34966`): spec 830 files pass; spec, runtime and service-automation typecheck 0; ablation 1/20 vitest red plus 3 test-typecheck problems; 85/85 derived gates exit 0 with `--ran` 0 NOT-MEASURED; `check-changeset-no-major` exit 0 with the body and 1 for the control.
  - The delta to this head is TSDoc, one doc-pin line and one changeset sentence. CI on the merged tree is green, including Test Core and every Type Check lane.
- **Contract review:**
  - 6762357312: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, PASS, no must-fix. Should-fix 1 (the "own item" inference, false in a multi-package artifact, because `judgeJobPull` finds the mapping across every `packages[]` body) was verified by the seat in the tree and fixed.
  - Delta 6762454953 on this head: PASS. Should-fix 1 and nit 3 are closed.
- **Declarations:** `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, `@objectstack/spec` patch. This matches the `.changeset/31734` precedent for the same key on the ownership-queue reads. `Skills-docs: none` (nothing an author writes changes). Body r1 drops the `appId` wording in step with the TSDoc.
- **Accepted deviations:**
  - Nit 2: "exactly as today" names today's bare read, which differs from D3's caller-less read once #32071 lands. It is true at this head and is reworded with the reader on #32071.
  - The changeset keeps the short form "a refusal naming every candidate" (prose).
  - The branch is not re-merged with `main`: 3 first-parent commits behind, none touching `packages/spec/src/contracts/`, and CI ran the merged tree green.
- **Carried:** #32071's pull half: the runtime binder passes the package that declares the job, and `connector-pull.ts` reads by D3. It must measure the multi-package case for its own `Narrowing:` line and reword the absent-value sentence. #31700 waits on that reader.
- **Red-line review (epic ADR-0150):** the diff publishes a type and a doc, and no behaviour. No reader exists at this head, so no one-holder answer can change.
- **Landing:** not governed (`check-governed-merges --pr 32114`: 104 lines, 0 governed paths), so Tier S. The relay landing stroke is refused in this session by the auto-mode classifier ("Merge Without Review", first met on PR #32034). The maintainer readies this PR and enables auto-merge, or allows the stroke.
